title: Tools and resources
subtitle: Keep the right tools close without letting tools replace reasoning.

isi: A calculator, reference sheet, or graphing tool is most useful after you identify the relationship in the problem. First decide what the question is asking; then choose the tool that reduces unnecessary work.

isi.title: A good tool decision
isi.content: If a question asks when two quantities are equal, model the relationship first. For example, if \(f(x) = 2x + 3\) and \(g(x) = 11\), the useful question is \(2x + 3 = 11\), not simply which button to press.

items.title: Formula notes
items.content: Keep formulas with one example and one common trap.

items.title: Error log
items.content: Record the reason a choice failed, not only the correct answer.

items.title: Timed sets
items.content: Use short sets to practice switching between question types.

isi: Separate official information from tutor notes and personal shortcuts. When a policy, schedule, or test feature matters, verify it with the current official source before relying on it.

latihan.question: What should happen before choosing a calculator strategy?
discussion: The relationship tells you whether a calculator, graph, estimation, or algebraic manipulation is the most efficient next step.

additionalPractice.question: Before solving a new SAT Information question, what should you identify first?
additionalPractice.answer: Identify what the question is asking and the information that matters.
discussion: Read the question carefully and name the quantity, claim, or skill being tested.
Then choose a representation or strategy that matches the information given.
